questions.subject: English Language
questions.text:
Nigeria's power sector has struggled for decades to supply reliable electricity to homes and businesses, forcing many to rely on private generators as a costly and polluting alternative. Successive governments have attempted reforms, including the privatisation of the generation and distribution companies once held solely by the state. Proponents argue that private ownership brings efficiency and fresh investment that a cash-strapped government could never provide alone. What is the closest meaning of the word 'elusive' as used in the final sentence of the passage?
questions.explanation: 'Elusive' describes something that is hard to attain or achieve, fitting the context of reliable power remaining out of reach.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: He suggested that she ______ the report before submission.

We bought apples oranges and bananas.
We bought apples oranges, and bananas.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'The committee members, together with the chairman, ___ arriving shortly.'
questions.explanation: 'The committee members' is technically plural, but many style guides note the true subject focus can shift; however, using standard subject-verb agreement rules, the core subject 'the chairman' (singular, since 'together with' introduces a parenthetical) governs the verb — 'is arriving' is correct.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: His ARROGANT manner offended many guests.

questions.subject: English Language

The three finalists were; John, Mary, and Peter.
The three finalists were: John, Mary, and Peter.
The three finalists were John, Mary, and Peter

questions.subject: English Language

questions.subject: English Language

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text:
Nigeria's power sector has struggled for decades to supply reliable electricity to homes and businesses, forcing many to rely on private generators as a costly and polluting alternative. Successive governments have attempted reforms, including the privatisation of the generation and distribution companies once held solely by the state. Proponents argue that private ownership brings efficiency and fresh investment that a cash-strapped government could never provide alone. Sceptics counter that the reforms have simply replaced one set of problems with another, since many distribution companies still lack the capital to maintain and expand the ageing national grid. Until significant new generation capacity comes online and the grid itself is modernised, most analysts agree that widespread, reliable power will remain elusive.

What do proponents of privatisation argue, according to the passage?
options: It brings efficiency and investment the government could not provide alone
It has completely solved Nigeria's power problems
It eliminates the need for any further investment
It has made electricity available for free
questions.explanation: The passage states proponents argue privatisation 'brings efficiency and fresh investment that a cash-strapped government could never provide alone.'
